'''Tie''': {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No data}} | title = [[List of governors of Florida|Governor]] | before_election = [[Rick Scott]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Ron DeSantis]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsFL}} The '''2018 Florida gubernatorial election''' was held on November 6, 2018, to elect the next [[List of governors of Florida|governor of Florida]], alongside an [[2018 United States Senate election in Florida|election]] to the [[United States Senate]], [[2018 United States House of Representatives elections in Florida|elections]] to the [[United States House of Representatives]], and other [[2018 Florida elections|state and local elections]]. Incumbent two-term [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Governor [[Rick Scott]] was term-limited and could not run for a third term, and he successfully [[2018 United States Senate election in Florida|ran for Florida's Class I Senate seat]]. Republican U.S. representative [[Ron DeSantis]] narrowly defeated [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] mayor of Tallahassee [[Andrew Gillum]] for the governorship, in what some considered an [[Upset (competition)|upset]]. The candidate filing deadline was June 22, 2018, and primary elections were held on August 28. Florida uses a closed primary process, in which the selection of each party's candidates for a general election is limited to registered members of that party;{{cite web|url=https://ballotpedia.org/Florida_gubernatorial_and_lieutenant_gubernatorial_election,_2018|title=Florida gubernatorial and lieutenant gubernatorial election, 2018|website=Ballotpedia|access-date=March 28, 2018}} Gillum won the Democratic primary and DeSantis the Republican primary.{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/elections/results/florida-governor |title=Florida Governor Election Results: Andrew Gillum vs. Ron DeSantis |work=The New York Times |access-date=2018-11-07}} The close margin mandated a machine recount, which had a deadline of November 15, 2018. After the recount was complete, DeSantis was certified as the winner. Gillum conceded on November 17. DeSantis's victory marked the sixth straight election in which Florida elected a Republican to the governorship, and the third in a row that neither candidate received over 50% of the vote. With a margin of 0.4%, this election was the closest race of the [[2018 United States gubernatorial elections|2018 gubernatorial election cycle]], and also the closest gubernatorial election in Florida history. Gillum became the first Democrat to win [[Duval County, Florida|Duval County]] since [[1986 Florida gubernatorial election|1986]] and [[Seminole County, Florida|Seminole County]] since [[1990 Florida gubernatorial election|1990]], while DeSantis became the first Republican gubernatorial candidate to win [[Jefferson County, Florida|Jefferson County]] since [[1884 Florida gubernatorial If the margin was below 0.25% after machine recount, [[Ken Detzner]], the [[Secretary of State of Florida|secretary of state of Florida]], would commission a manual recount of over-votes and under-votes.{{Cite web |last=Levy |first=Adam |date=November 10, 2018 |title=The Florida recount is now official. Here's how it will work |url=https://lebanon-express.com/news/national/govt-and-politics/the-florida-recount-is-now-official-heres-how-it-will-work/article_7207331d-2e61-5eea-b3d4-cd24a525953c.html |access-date=January 10, 2021 |website=Lebanon Express |archive-date=August 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220804152840/https://lebanon-express.com/news/national/govt-and-politics/the-florida-recount-is-now-official-heres-how-it-will-work/article_7207331d-2e61-5eea-b3d4-cd24a525953c.html |url-status=dead }} However, after the recount was complete, DeSantis' margin was 0.40%; therefore, he was certified the winner. Gillum conceded on November 17.{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Jessica |title=Democrat Andrew Gillum Concedes Florida Governor's Race To Ron DeSantis |url=https://www.npr.org/2018/11/17/668321180/andrew-gillum-concedes-floridas-governor-s-race-to-ron-desantis |website=NPR |access-date=23 March 2022 |language=en |date=17 November 2018}} DeSantis narrowly won due to strong Republican turnout in several counties in Central/Southwest Florida that had helped Trump pull off a win in 2016, exceeding Rick Scott's 2014 margin of victory in Pasco, Polk, Volusia, Lee, Sarasota, and Brevard, among others. DeSantis also put in a great deal of effort to prevent losing Miami-Dade by too big of a margin, firing up older Cuban exiles and making overtures to Venezuelans, Nicaraguans, and other non Cuban-Hispanics by painting Gillum as a socialist while being boosted by Jeanette Núñez's presence on the ticket. Gillum won the county overwhelmingly (and performed strongly in non-Cuban Hispanic areas), but DeSantis succeeded in keeping Gillum's numbers down, losing by 167,377 votes compared to Trump's 290,147 loss two years earlier. On November 10, 2022, former president [[Donald Trump]] claimed on his [[Truth Social]] page that he had prematurely ended the recount to prevent DeSantis and Senate candidate [[Rick Scott]] from losing, under the unsubstantiated belief that [[Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election#Stop the Steal|ballots for them were being removed]].{{cite web | url=https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/109322011642437369 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221111003430/https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/109322011642437369 | archive-date=November 11, 2022 | title=Truth Social }} Florida Commissioner of Agriculture [[Nikki Fried]] asked Attorney General [[Merrick Garland]] to investigate.{{cite news |author= |date=November 14, 2022 |title=US Attorney General asked to investigate Trump claims regarding 2018 Florida elections |url=https://www.wesh.com/article/us-attorney-general-trump-2018-florida-elections/41954543 |work=WESH Channel 2 |access-date=November 24, 2022}} [[Sarah Isgur]], the spokeswoman of the [[Department of Justice]] from 2017 to 2019, has said that it "never happened,"{{cite news |last=Gregorian |first=Dareh |date=November 11, 2022 |title=Trump claims he sent the FBI to Florida to stop voter fraud in 2018. Officials say no such thing happened. |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump/trump-claims-sent-fbi-florida-stop-voter-fraud-2018-officials-say-no-t-rcna56809 |work=NBC News |access-date=November 24, 2022}} a position which was supported by other former Department of Justice officials.{{Cite web |last2=Barber |first1=Sonam|last1= Sheth|first2= C. Ryan |title='Bogus,' 'ridiculous,' and 'made-up crap': DOJ veterans throw cold water on Trump's claim that he 'sent in the FBI' to help Ron DeSantis |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/doj-veterans-react-trump-fbi-desantis-2018-election-2022-11 |access-date=2022-11-17 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US}} Broward County Commissioner [[Steven Geller]] agreed that no interference took place.{{cite news |last=Kochi |first=Sudiksha |date=November 14, 2022 |title=Fact check: Trump falsely claims he saved Ron DeSantis from ballot stealing in 2018 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2022/11/14/fact-check-trumps-false-claim-he-stopped-steal-2018-desantis-florida/10697871002/ |work=USA Today |access-date=November 24, 2022}} ===Voter demographics=== {| class="wikitable" |+Edison Research exit poll !
